title: Story of King Bakhtzaman (Español)
summary: Bakhtiyar recounted the history of King Bakhtzaman of Yemen: [ES]
full_text:
Bakhtiyar recounted the history of King Bakhtzaman of Yemen:

'A military rebellion led by an ambitious general overthrew King Bakhtzaman, driving the righteous monarch into the desert with his queen and young infant. Wandering across trackless dunes, the king lost his camel, his water, and was captured by desert brigands who separated him from his family.

In his darkest hour, chained in a foreign port, Bakhtzaman did not curse heaven or surrender to despair. He said: "The heavens that gave me a crown can take it away, and the providence that sustains the sparrow in the storm can restore the wanderer. I place my soul in the hands of the Merciful."

He worked as an honest porter in the docks for seven years, conducting himself with such integrity that the city merchants appointed him guardian of the harbor storehouses.

When the tyrannical usurper in Yemen died, leaving the kingdom in civil strife, the people rose in revolt, demanding the return of their beloved King Bakhtzaman.

Envoys were dispatched to search the ports of the East. They discovered their former monarch working in the harbor, his hands calloused by labor and his spirit purified by faith!

Bakhtzaman was escorted back to Yemen, joyfully reunited with his queen and son who had been preserved in safety, and restored to his throne amidst national celebrations, proving that trust in providence outlasts the darkest exile.'
moral: Unwavering faith and adherence to justice restore the rightful ruler to his throne. [ES]
